statement.p: Use implicit differentiation to find the points where the parabola defined by x^{2}-2xy+y^{2}+6x-10y+29 = 0 has horizontal and vertical tangent lines.
The parabola has horizontal tangent lines at the .
The parabola has vertical tangent lines at the point(s) .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives 2x-2y-2x\, \frac{dy}{dx}+2y\, \frac{dy}{dx}+6-10\, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, or (y-x-5) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = y-x-3, and so \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y-x-3}{y-x-5}. The tangent line to the parabola is horizontal where \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, i.e., where x - y = -3. The equation of the parabola can be written in the form \left(x-y\right)^{2}+6\mathopen{}\left(x-y\right)+29-4y = 0, and x - y = -3 gives 20 = 4y, or y = 5, and x = 2. Hence, the tangent line to the parabola is horizontal at the point \left(2,5\right) and nowhere else.

The tangent line the the parabola is vertical where 0 = \frac{dx}{dy} = \frac{y-x-5}{y-x-3}, i.e., where x - y = -5. Together with the last displayed equation of the parabola, this gives 24 - 4y = 0, or y = 6, and x = 1. Hence, the tangent line to the parabola is vertical at the point \left(1,6\right) and nowhere else.
